research_rationale: EO 11320 (31 FR 15789, signed 1966-12-12) has one operative paragraph: it designates the Secretary of State, and when designated by the Secretary the Under Secretary of State, to exercise the President's rulemaking authority under section 7 of the Foreign Gifts and Decorations Act of 1966, and requires the rules to be published in the Federal Register. The held text is the Federal Register OCR text layer (original_representation_unverified), whole order bounded in the held file. EO 12553 of 1986-02-25 (51 FR 7237, issue of 1986-03-03), whose text is held, revokes EO 11320 by listing it by number and subject; no earlier revocation, supersession or own-terms end appears in the held later-events chain or the OFR catalog search, which records EO 12553 as the revoking order. The command is therefore not in force on the 2026-10-14 cutoff.
savings_reason: EO 12553 revokes the listed orders and any amendments thereto and contains no savings clause. The order was a delegation of rulemaking authority; rules the Secretary of State had already prescribed under it were the Secretary's own acts, not commands of the order, and are not shown by held text to depend on the order's continued life. The order's own text states no term of years. The 22 CFR 1203.735 leads that cite the order are machine snippets only, with no held legal-text slice.
conflict_resolutions: {"NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW": "The two current-law leads are 22 CFR 1203.735-203 and 22 CFR 1203.735-305 (machine snippets of eCFR text amended through 2026-10-13; no legal-text slice is held). The 203 snippet cites E.O. 11320 as the authority under which regulations were promulgated, a historical authority citation to a revoked order. A regulation's citation of an order does not keep the order's delegation in force, and EO 12553 expressly revoked it in 1986, so the provisional NO stands. No current command of the order is shown."}
earlier_end_check: Searched held later orders and the OFR catalog for EO 11320 by number: the only hit is the EO 12553 revocation (1986-02-25). The order states no own-terms end. Any statute replacing the 1966 Act (5 U.S.C. 7342, named only in a machine CFR snippet, no held text) names no executive order and under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments is disclosed as an unestablished earlier candidate, not an end.
scope_check: Single clause: the whole order is one paragraph of delegation plus a publication requirement; the held text shows no other operative sentence. EO 12553 revokes the order as a whole, so there is no partial survival.
independent_command_check: Nothing in the order is independent of the delegation: the Federal Register publication sentence applies only to rules made under that delegation, and no other command exists. No report or deadline is involved.
savings_check: EO 12553 has no savings clause; see the savings reason. No pending proceeding or accrued right is shown by held text.
